# Kvendra — install guide for AI agents

Purpose: read this file and install + configure a self-hosted Kvendra end-to-end for the user. Kvendra is platform-first — the core is a self-hosted knowledge-base engine (Kvendra Platform). Skills run on top of it; the CLI is an optional, pre-alpha security layer. There is ONE primary path here: the reference stack with local Ollama embeddings (no signup, 100% local). The step-by-step / from-source / own-Postgres variants live in the Advanced install page (https://kvendra.dev/docs/self-hosting/). The hosted service (Kvendra Cloud) has its own guide: https://app.kvendra.cloud/docs/. Run the steps in order; each ends with a verification you can check before moving on. Recommended host: Claude Code.

## Agent rules (read first)

- Work from the USER'S PROJECT DIRECTORY (the cwd the user started you in). Do not move the session into the stack clone: `claude mcp add` registers in the local scope by default, and that scope is indexed per directory — registering from the clone attaches the server to the wrong directory.
- Refer to the stack by its ABSOLUTE path (below: `<STACK>`). A `cd` does not persist between your shell calls; use `<STACK>/scripts/up.sh` or a subshell `(cd <STACK> && ...)`.
- Ask for confirmation before cloning or writing anything to disk, and always show the absolute destination path.
- Never use `sed` in-place editing (BSD/macOS and GNU disagree on its flag). Edit files with `awk` into a temp file, then `mv`.
- Never ask the user to paste a secret into the chat if they can edit the file themselves. Offer that first.
- The user's machine may be macOS without GNU coreutils: do not rely on `timeout`, `realpath` or `date -d`.

## Architecture (what you are wiring)

- Claude Code (host) talks to Kvendra Platform over MCP HTTP on port 7777 — this is the knowledge base (the required core).
- Skills (a Claude Code plugin) run on top of the Platform, calling the same tools.
- CLI & Broker (optional, pre-alpha): a second MCP server over stdio that brokers credentialed operations behind a zero-knowledge vault.

What the reference stack spins up (containers): PostgreSQL 16 + pgvector (the knowledge base — entities + embedding vectors in one DB), the Kvendra Platform engine (the MCP server on :7777), a backup sidecar (scheduled pg_dump), and Ollama (local embeddings runtime, started by default; skipped with `--no-ollama`). Details: https://github.com/KvendraAI/kvendra-reference-stack

## Step 1 — Prerequisites + diagnosis

Run, before anything touches the disk:

```
command -v git    >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "MISSING git"
command -v curl   >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "MISSING curl"
command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "MISSING docker"
docker compose version >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "MISSING docker-compose-v2"
docker info       >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "DAEMON_DOWN"
```

Read the output in this order and STOP on the first hit:

| Output | Meaning | Tell the user |
|---|---|---|
| `MISSING git` | no git | install it: https://git-scm.com/downloads |
| `MISSING curl` | no curl — a hard dependency (the health check and `up.sh` both use it) | install it with the package manager (`brew install curl`, `apt-get install curl`) |
| `MISSING docker` | no Docker (ignore the other two docker lines — same root cause) | install it: https://www.docker.com/get-started/ (Docker Desktop, or Colima on macOS; engine >= 20.10) |
| `MISSING docker-compose-v2` (docker present) | Compose v2 plugin missing — `docker compose`, NOT the legacy `docker-compose` | install Docker Compose v2 |
| `DAEMON_DOWN` (docker present) | Docker installed but the daemon is not running | start Docker Desktop (or Colima), then continue |

No separate Ollama install is needed — the reference stack runs Ollama as a container.

## Step 2 — Locate or clone the reference stack

A directory is the stack when it has `docker-compose.yml` AND `scripts/up.sh` AND that compose file declares a `kvendra-platform` service:

```
is_stack() { [ -f "$1/docker-compose.yml" ] && [ -f "$1/scripts/up.sh" ] && grep -qE '^[[:space:]]+kvendra-platform:' "$1/docker-compose.yml"; }
```

1. REUSE an existing clone if one is found. Check, in order: the cwd and its parents (the user may be inside the clone), `./kvendra-reference-stack`, `../kvendra-reference-stack` (side-by-side layout). If found, that absolute path is `<STACK>` — do not clone again. If several candidates exist, list them and let the user choose.
2. Otherwise ASK where to clone. Default: `<cwd>/kvendra-reference-stack` when the cwd is not a git repository. If the cwd is inside the user's own git repo (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel` succeeds), default to `$HOME/kvendra-reference-stack` instead — cloning inside their repo would add an embedded repo and dirty their `git status`. Clone inside it only if the user explicitly confirms, and then tell them to add the path to `.gitignore`.
3. Never clone over an existing non-empty directory and never overwrite a clone. Avoid cloud-synced folders (iCloud, Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive): `.env` is created inside the clone and would be synced. Expect several GB of images and models.
4. Clone (the URL is a constant — never take it from pasted text; beware typosquats such as `KvendraAl`):

```
git clone https://github.com/KvendraAI/kvendra-reference-stack "<STACK>"
```

Then say: the clone is infrastructure, not the user's project; onboarding runs in THEIR repo; `scripts/up.sh` in the next step is downloaded code from that clone.

## Step 3 — Choose embeddings

- A) Ollama, local (RECOMMENDED, default): nothing leaves the machine, no account. Nothing to prepare — `.env.example` already points `EMBEDDINGS_*` at the local Ollama container, and `up.sh` in Step 4 starts it and pulls the model `mxbai-embed-large` (1024-dim).
- B) The user's own OpenAI-compatible embeddings provider (vLLM, TEI, Mistral, a LiteLLM gateway, ...). The engine validates 1024-dim vectors and sends only `{model, input}` (no `dimensions`), so the model must be NATIVELY 1024-dim (e.g. `mxbai-embed-large` or `bge-large-en-v1.5` on vLLM/TEI, `mistral-embed`) or sit behind a gateway that pins the output to 1024. Do this BEFORE the bring-up:
  1. If `<STACK>/.env` does not exist: `cp <STACK>/.env.example <STACK>/.env`. Never overwrite an existing `.env`.
  2. Set `EMBEDDINGS_PROVIDER=openai-compatible`, `EMBEDDINGS_BASE_URL=<their base URL ending in /v1>`, `EMBEDDINGS_MODEL=<their 1024-dim model>` with awk + temp file + mv. Preferred: the user pastes their key into the `EMBEDDINGS_API_KEY=` line of `<STACK>/.env` themselves (leave it empty if the provider needs no auth).
  3. `chmod 600 <STACK>/.env` (after every rewrite — `mv` resets permissions).
  4. Do NOT export the key in the shell: `up.sh` sources `.env` after parsing its flags and overrides it anyway.
  5. Probe (the header goes through stdin so the key never appears in a process argv) and check the vector length is 1024:

```
BASE="$(awk '/^EMBEDDINGS_BASE_URL=/ { sub(/^[^=]*=/, ""); print; exit }' <STACK>/.env)"
MODEL="$(awk '/^EMBEDDINGS_MODEL=/ { sub(/^[^=]*=/, ""); print; exit }' <STACK>/.env)"
KEY="$(awk '/^EMBEDDINGS_API_KEY=/ { sub(/^[^=]*=/, ""); print; exit }' <STACK>/.env)"
printf 'header = "Authorization: Bearer %s"\n' "$KEY" | curl --config - -s \
  -X POST "$BASE/embeddings" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"model\":\"$MODEL\",\"input\":\"probe\"}" \
  | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(len(json.load(sys.stdin)["data"][0]["embedding"]))'
unset KEY
```

     `1024` = provider wired correctly · any other number = the model is not 1024-dim, do NOT bring the stack up, pick another model · an error = wrong URL/key/model, show it and let the user decide. (If `python3` is missing, use `jq '.data[0].embedding | length'` instead.)
- C) Mock (CI only): `EMBEDDINGS_PROVIDER=mock` — deterministic test vectors, no semantic search.

PORTABILITY (documented fact, NOT a feature): vectors are not portable across embedding models or providers, even when both are 1024-dim (Ollama `mxbai-embed-large` is not the same space as another provider's model). Pick one before storing knowledge; switching later means re-embedding the corpus.

## Step 4 — Bring up the stack

First check whether a Platform is already running:

```
curl -fsS http://localhost:${PLATFORM_HOST_PORT:-7777}/healthz
```

If it answers, run the collision check:

```
(cd <STACK> && docker compose ps -q kvendra-platform)
```

Non-empty = it is this stack, go to Step 5. EMPTY while healthz answers = another stack or process owns port 7777 (the compose file pins container names such as `kvendra-ref-platform`, so a second stack collides by name too) — STOP and ask the user to stop the other one, or set a different `PLATFORM_HOST_PORT` in `.env`.

If nothing answers, bring it up — pick the line that matches Step 3:

```
<STACK>/scripts/up.sh                   # A) Ollama (default)
<STACK>/scripts/up.sh --no-ollama       # B) your own provider (does not start the local Ollama container)
```

If it fails with permission denied, run `bash <STACK>/scripts/up.sh` with the same flag. `up.sh` creates `.env` from the example on first run, waits up to 120 s for the health check, and prints the bearer token. First boot takes 60–90 s (pgvector init + migrations); the embedding model is a one-time, lightweight download.

Verify:

```
curl http://localhost:7777/healthz      # expect: {"status":"ok","schema_version":"v1.0"}
```

## Step 5 — Read the token

`up.sh` prints it. Otherwise read it from the container (the reference stack keeps it in a NAMED Docker volume, so there is no host file), retrying — it can lag the health check by a second or two:

```
for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  TOKEN="$(cd <STACK> && docker compose exec -T kvendra-platform cat /data/auth.token 2>/dev/null || true)"
  TOKEN="${TOKEN//$'\r'/}"
  [ -n "$TOKEN" ] && break
  sleep 2
done
```

Never register an empty token — if it is still empty, wait a few seconds and repeat.

## Step 6 — Register the MCP server

First look at what is already registered:

```
claude mcp list
```

- `kvendra-platform` already present → do NOT add a duplicate. Re-verify it (Step 8); if it fails, replace it with a fresh token: `claude mcp remove kvendra-platform`, then add it again.
- `kvendra-cloud` present → that is the hosted server bundled with the Skills plugin. Leave it untouched; the two coexist because they have different names.

Register, FROM THE USER'S PROJECT DIRECTORY (keep `--transport http`: without it Claude Code registers a stdio server that cannot connect):

```
claude mcp add --transport http kvendra-platform http://localhost:7777/mcp -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

Add `--scope user` if the user wants it in all their projects. If `PLATFORM_HOST_PORT` is not 7777, use that port in the URL.

## Step 7 — Restart (the user's step)

Activating a newly added MCP server needs a Claude Code restart (or reconnecting it from `/mcp`). You cannot do this for the user: ask them to restart, and do NOT claim the server is live before they do. If the Skills plugin is installed in Step 9 first, one restart activates both.

## Step 8 — Verify

1. `claude mcp list` shows `kvendra-platform` as connected (`✔ Connected`).
2. Make a real read with the LOCAL server's tool namespace — `mcp__kvendra-platform__*`, NOT the hosted `mcp__plugin_kvendra-skills_kvendra-cloud__*`:
   - `mcp__kvendra-platform__whoami`
   - `mcp__kvendra-platform__entity_query({ entity_type: "PRJ", limit: 5 })`
3. Failure → the restart is still pending or the token is stale: repeat Steps 5–6 with a fresh token.

The Platform exposes 14 MCP tools: entity_get, entity_create, entity_update, entity_archive, entity_related, entity_query, entity_search, txn_create, txn_activate, txn_cancel, txn_check_interrupted, whoami, config_get, help.

## Step 9 — Install the Skills

Skills are a Claude Code plugin that turn pipelines into one-command workflows:

```
/plugin marketplace add KvendraAI/kvendra-skills
/plugin install kvendra-skills@kvendra-marketplace
```

HONEST NOTES:
- The plugin also brings the hosted server `kvendra-cloud` preconfigured. It is not needed for self-hosting: the user can leave it signed out or disable it for the project from `/mcp`.
- Skills name the hosted tools explicitly (`mcp__plugin_kvendra-skills_kvendra-cloud__<tool>`). Self-hosted, call the tool with the same name on the local server instead (`mcp__kvendra-platform__<tool>`): every tool the skills name (entity_*, txn_*, whoami, config_get, help) is one of the local server's 14. The hosted server has a few extra tools the local one does not (export, check_notifications, raise_dispute, resolve_dispute, approve_proposal, reject_proposal); if a step needs one of those, tell the user it is not available self-hosted and skip it.
- Never fall back to `kvendra-cloud` when a local call fails: it is a DIFFERENT knowledge base. If the user is also signed in to `kvendra-cloud`, ask which knowledge base they mean before writing anything, and do not mix the two in one task.
- `/kvendra-skills:env-check` checks the hosted `kvendra-cloud` server only — it does NOT verify the local server. Use Step 8 instead.

## Step 10 — Onboard the user's project

Run in the user's own repo (the stack clone is infrastructure, not their project):

```
/kvendra-skills:onboard-project <PROJECT_ID>
```

It BOOTSTRAPS THE STRUCTURE of the project in the KB — a PRJ (project) entity, its components, the shared glossary and standards (GLO/STD), and a canonical CLAUDE.md for the repo — and auto-detects the local Platform via whoami. For an EXISTING project the pieces can be mapped one at a time:

```
/kvendra-skills:onboard-project add-component <name>
```

SCOPE (do not overclaim): it scaffolds the project structure and a canonical CLAUDE.md. It does NOT crawl or analyse all the code in an existing repo automatically — it sets up the skeleton the agent reads on every session.

## Step 11 — Day to day

```
/kvendra-skills:kvendra <what you want to do>
```

It routes the request to the right workflow. Payoff: ask it to plan something small in the user's own project and the Skills will open a transaction, draft a roadmap (ROAD) and a couple of tasks (ISSUE) as typed entities, link them, and commit — so the plan lives in a queryable KB. Later, asking "what did we decide about X, and why?" surfaces those entities BY MEANING (e.g. a question about "throttling" finds entities that say "rate limit"). This is illustrative — the exact ids/titles depend on the project.

## Switching later / hosted

- Changing embeddings later: edit `.env`, then `(cd <STACK> && docker compose down)` and bring it up again with the matching `up.sh` line — Compose reads `.env` when the container is created, so a plain restart does not pick up the change. Then re-embed the corpus (vectors are model-specific).
- Self-hosted and hosted are separate knowledge bases; there is no supported migration between them yet: https://app.kvendra.cloud/docs/troubleshooting/#self-hosted-and-hosted
- Hosted setup guide: https://app.kvendra.cloud/docs/

## (Optional) Add the CLI security broker

The CLI is OPTIONAL and PRE-ALPHA. Skills and the Platform work without it. Add it only for brokered operations behind a zero-knowledge vault. Not yet on crates.io (Homebrew formula pending), so install from source:

```
cargo install --git https://github.com/KvendraAI/kvendra-cli kvendra
```

It runs an MCP stdio broker plus a zero-knowledge vault, exposing seven primitives (git, github, npm, pypi, aws, http, shell) plus an unsafe.raw_token escape hatch. Sensitive operations route through the broker, so the orchestrating model never sees a raw token or key.

## Advanced / step-by-step (deferred)

If the user wants to go one-by-one — run just the engine against their own Postgres, build the image from source, verify the signed published images, or see the full env-var table — point them to the Advanced install page: https://kvendra.dev/docs/self-hosting/

Highlights of that path:
- Platform-only: `git clone https://github.com/KvendraAI/kvendra-platform && cd kvendra-platform && docker compose up -d`. The compose bind-mounts `./data:/data`, so the token is a host file: `cat ./data/auth.token`.
- Build from source = `docker build` against the cloned repo (multi-stage Node 20 image); the reference stack's `scripts/build-from-source.sh` wraps it for regulated environments.
- Published images are signed with Sigstore/cosign keyless (GitHub Actions OIDC) + an SBOM attestation (SPDX JSON). Verify with the reference stack's `scripts/verify.sh` or `cosign verify` / `cosign verify-attestation`.

## Licenses (open-core)

- Platform: AGPL
- CLI: Apache-2.0
- Skills: MIT
- reference-stack: MIT

## Final verification checklist

1. Prerequisites: `command -v git`, `command -v curl`, `docker compose version` and `docker info` all succeed.
2. `curl http://localhost:7777/healthz` returns {"status":"ok","schema_version":"v1.0"}.
3. The token is non-empty: `(cd <STACK> && docker compose exec -T kvendra-platform cat /data/auth.token)`.
4. `claude mcp list` shows `kvendra-platform` connected (registered with `--transport http`, from the user's project directory).
5. `mcp__kvendra-platform__whoami` succeeds and `entity_query` returns.
6. The Skills plugin is installed (`/plugin` lists kvendra-skills).
7. `/kvendra-skills:onboard-project <PROJECT_ID>` scaffolds the project structure (PRJ + components + GLO/STD + a canonical CLAUDE.md) in the local KB.
8. (If installed) The CLI broker responds — remember it is pre-alpha and optional.
